newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs trade listlessly ahead tankan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs trade listlessly ahead tankan.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures remained in a tight range on very low turnover on Monday, as players began their watch for the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s quarterly tankan survey.
Dealers said the market failed to react to comments by a BOJ official about the possibility of further failures at Japanese financial institutions.
"The JGB and Euroyen traders are just sitting on their hands, waiting for the tankan right now," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
He said the market had largely priced in a tankan showing limited improvement in Japanese business sentiment during the third quarter.

"Personally, I feel JGBs could see more upside. They should be higher than this fundamentally. There are rollovers and end-of-year redemptions by the Trust Fund Bureau," he said, adding that December JGBs could test 126.00 again.

He said June Euroyen should keep to a range of 99.12-99.24 ahead of the tankan. It was quoted at 99.21 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close at 99.18. December JGBs ended at 124.69 against their previous 124.65.
A trader with a European bank said December JGBs were unlikely to climb back above 125.50.
Eurodollar futures were glued within a one-tick band on a lack of fresh interest. March finished at 94.50 against its IMM close at 94.49 on turnover of a paltry 1,640 lots.
"I don't think this market's going to sell off without a major shock. But we've reached a level where it's not that easy to buy either. All the good news is priced in," said the European bank dealer.
